'''Beta Kappa Chi''' ('''{{lang|grc|ΒΚΧ}}''') is an American collegiate [[honor society]] that recognizes academic achievement in the fields of [[natural science]] and [[mathematics]]. It was established in 1923 at [[Lincoln University (Pennsylvania)|Lincoln University]], a [[Historically black university|historically Black university]] near [[Oxford, Pennsylvania]]. It has established more than 65 chapters in the United States, and is a member of the [[Association of College Honor Societies]].

== History ==
'''Beta Kappa Chi Scientific Society''' was founded by science students and faculty at [[Lincoln University (Pennsylvania)|Lincoln University]] on January 31, 1923.<ref name="Baird's">{{Bairds20|pages=VI-18–19}}</ref><ref name=":2">Williams Joseph L. "[https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2616064/?page=1 Beta Kappa Chi: A Challenge Not To Be Ignored]." ''Journal of the National Medical Association'', vol. ''37, no.'' 1 (January 1945): 26. via PubMed Central.</ref><ref name=":5">Williams, Joseph L. "{{JSTOR|4604825}} Betta Kappa Chi Honorary Scientific Society]." ''Bios'' vol. 15, no. 3 (October 1944): 137–139.</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite book |last=Bond |first=Horace Mann |url=https://credo.library.umass.edu/view/pageturn/mums411-b008-f105/#page/7/mode/1up |title=How Beta Kappa Chi Began (Letter to Dr. Joseph L. Williams) |date=November 6, 1943 |publisher=Beta Kappa Chi |via=University of Massachusetts Amherst Library}}</ref> Its faculty supporters were [[Harold Fetter Grimm]], head of the department of biology; Arthur E. James, professor of chemistry' and [[Walter Livingston Wright|Walter Livingstone Wright]], professor of mathematics.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Our History |url=https://www.betakappachi.org/about-us/our-history |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=Beta Kappa Chi}}</ref><ref name=":7" />

Its 24 charter members were:<ref name=":5"/><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":9">{{Cite news |date=1973-03-31 |title=Lincoln Sponsors Golden Anniversary of Beta Kappa Chi |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/new-pittsburgh-courier-lincoln-sponsors/154913259/ |access-date=2024-09-08 |work=New Pittsburgh Courier |pages=11 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>
{{columns-list|colwidth=12em|

* Lawrence N. Brown
* Walter C. Coles

* Adelphus N. Gordon
* James W. Grimes
* Irving S. Hamer

* [[Hildrus Poindexter]]

Six of its charter members became medical doctors, one became a dentist, and another became a college president.<ref name=":5"/><ref name=":7" />

The charter members created a constitution and selected the society's keys and symbols.<ref name=":7" /> Initially, Beta Kappa Chi operated as a local science club.<ref name=":2" /> Its first guest speaker was [[Ernest Everett Just]], a biologist from [[Howard University]].<ref name=":5"/><ref name=":7" />

It became a national organization on May 8, 1926, with the establishment of the Beta chapter at [[West Virginia State College]].<ref name=":5"/><ref name=":2" /> Beta Kappa Chi Honorary Scientific Society was incorporated in 1929.<ref name=":5"/> Its purpose was to encourage and advance scientific education, research, and the dissemination of scientific knowledge.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=Constitution and By-Laws of Beta Kappa Chi Honorary Scientific Society |url=https://credo.library.umass.edu/view/pageturn/mums411-b008-f105/#page/9/mode/1up |access-date=September 8, 2024 |website=University of Massachusetts Amherst Library}}</ref><ref name=":9" /> Chapters were limited to accredited "grade A" colleges and universities.<ref name=":8" />

Next'','' Gamma chapter was established at [[Howard University]].<ref name=":2" /> By 1936, there were eight chapters. The society expanded to other historically black colleges and universities in the United States through 1941.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":5" /> However, the organization almost collapsed in 1941, surviving by the re-establishment of the Delta chapter at [[Johnson C. Smith University]] by its local science club and by the recruitment activities by members of the Alpha chapter.<ref name=":5"/><ref name=":6">{{Cite journal |date=May 1943 |title=Chapter News |url=https://credo.library.umass.edu/view/pageturn/mums411-b008-f105/#page/3/mode/1up |journal=Beta Kappa Chi Scientific Society News-Letter |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=2–3 |via=University of Massachusetts Amherst Library}}</ref> Gamma chapter was reestablished in 1943.<ref name=":6" />

To increase organizational stability, the society added a faculty sponsor for each chapter.<ref name=":5"/> This helped stabilize all eight of the Beta Kappa Chi chapters and brought the addition of thirteen more chapters.<ref name=":5"/> A grand chapter was established to oversee the national organization and to support alumni engagement.<ref name=":5"/>

The society published its first newsletter, ''Beta Kappa Chi Scientific Society News Letter'', in May 1943; its name was changed to the current ''Beta Kappa Chi Bulletin'' with the third issue in May 1944.<ref name=":2" />

The society changed its name to Beta Kappa Chi National Honor Society in 1960.<ref name=":0" /> It was admitted to the [[Association of College Honor Societies]] in 1961.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=February 12, 2012 |title=Beta Kappa Chi Honor Society – Natural Sciences and Mathematics |url=http://www.achsnatl.org/society.asp?society=bkc |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120414201119/http://www.achsnatl.org/society.asp?society=bkc |archive-date=2012-04-14 |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=Association of College Honor Societies |via=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name=":9" /> Nearly every [[Historically black colleges and universities|historically Black college and university]] in the United States had a chapter of Beta Kappa Chi by 1965.<ref name=":0" />

As of 2024, Beta Kappa Chi honor society has 67 active chapters across the United States, and 66,000 members.<ref name="National Website">{{Cite web |title=Home |url=https://www.betakappachi.org/ |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=www.betakappachi.org}}</ref> It is a scholastic [[honor society]] that recognizes academic achievement among students in the fields of [[natural science]] and [[mathematics]].<ref name="Baird's" /><ref name=":1" /> It is the oldest mostly Black scientific organization in the United States.<ref name=":9" />

== Symbols ==
The motto of Beta Kappa Chi is <nowiki>''Science holds the Golden Key to the Royal Palace of Knowledge''</nowiki>.<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":11">{{Cite web |title=Ritual, Symbols and Colors |url=https://www.betakappachi.org/about-us/ritual-symbols-and-colors |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=Beta Kappa Chi}}</ref> The meaning of the Greek letters Beta Kappa Chi are only known to the society's members, but represent its motto.<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":11" /> Its colors are golden yellow and [[royal blue]].<ref name=":11" /><ref name="Baird's" />

The Beta Kappa Chi key designed by charter member John Martyne Howe.<ref name=":7" /> Its key is shaped like a [[benzene ring]] with the Greek letters {{lang|grc|ΒΚΧ}} and a [[Clover|clover leaf]] above the {{lang|grc|Β}}, a [[Skull and crossbones (fraternities and sports)|skull and crossed bones]] above the {{lang|grc|Κ}}, and a circle above the {{lang|grc|Χ}}. There is a [[retort]] below the {{lang|grc|Β}}, a [[Balance scale|balance]] below the {{lang|grc|Κ}}, and scroll with stencils below the {{lang|grc|Χ}}.<ref name="Baird's" /><ref name=":8" /><ref name=":11" />

The symbols were selected by charter members Horace Bond, W. C. Coles, and Adolphus Gordon.<ref name=":7" /> The clover leaf symbolizes [[botany]],  the scull and crossed bones represent [[anatomy]], and the circle stands for [[astronomy]].<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":11" /> The retort represents chemistry,  balance is a symbol of physics, and the scroll with stencils represents mathematics.<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":11" />

Its publication is the ''Beta Kappa Chi Bulletin''.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

==Membership==
Membership is open to undergraduate and graduate students.<ref name=":1" /> Undergraduates are eligible for membership if they have completed 64 hours of college courses with 17 hours in the sciences, with a B average, and rank in the upper fifth of their class.<ref name=":1" /> Graduate students must have completed fifteen hours in the sciences with a mix of As and Bs.<ref name=":1" />

== Activities ==
Beta Kappa Chi has an annual national convention that includes research presentations by its members.<ref name=":1" /> This meeting is held in conjunction with the [[National Institute of Science]] in [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-04-29 |title=SU students present research at joint meeting of the National Institute of Science and Beta Kappa Chi Scientific Honors Society |url=https://www.subr.edu/news/su-students-present-research-at-joint-meeting-of-the-national-institute-of-science-and-beta-kappa-chi-scientific-honors-society |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=Southern University and A&M College |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":9" /><ref name=":10">{{Cite news |date=1952-05-02 |title=Many Colleges Represented at Join Science Convention at Prairie View |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-call-many-colleges-represented-at-jo/154916202/ |access-date=2024-09-08 |work=The Call |location=Kansas City, Missouri |pages=19 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> In 2017, it held a joint annual meeting with the [[National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases]] and the National Institute of Science.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Join NIAID at the Beta Kappa Chi & National Institute of Science joint annual meeting, 3/13-3/17 |url=https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USNIAID/bulletins/70748f |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases |language=en}}</ref>

==Chapters==
{{Main|List of Beta Kappa Chi chapters}}
As of 2024, Beta Kappa Chi honor society has 67 active chapters across the United States.<ref name="National Website" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=June 7, 2011 |title=Beta Kappa Chi Honor Society Chapters, ACHS |url=http://www.achsnatl.org/SocResults.asp?Society=bkc |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120414194017/http://www.achsnatl.org/SocResults.asp?Society=bkc |archive-date=2012-04-14 |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=Association of College Honor Societies |via=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Our Chapters |url=https://www.betakappachi.org/chapters/our-chapters |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=Beta Kappa Chi}}</ref> Chapters were assigned Greek letter names in alphabetical order until 1950; at that time Greek letter names were abolished and all chapters were named by their host institution.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Societies – Freddye T. Davy Honors College |url=https://home.hamptonu.edu/honors/societies/ |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=Hampton University |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Notable members==
* [[Horace Mann Bond]] (''Alpha''), president of [[Fort Valley State College]] and [[father]] of [[Civil rights movement|civil-rights]] leader [[Julian Bond]]<ref name=":5"/><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":9" />
* [[Ulysses Grant Dailey]] (''Alpha''), surgeon and  president of the [[National Medical Association]]<ref name=":2" />
* [[Harold Fetter Grimm]] (Alpha honorary), head of the department of biology and dean for fifty years at [[Lincoln University (Pennsylvania)|Lincoln University]]<ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Grim Hall |url=https://www.lincoln.edu/about/maps/campus-buildings/grim-hall.html |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=Lincoln University}}</ref>
* [[Mary Elliott Hill]], one of the earliest African-American women to become a [[chemist]]
* [[Robert S. Jason]] (''Alpha''), head of the department of pathology at the [[Howard University College of Medicine]]<ref name=":5"/><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":7" />
* [[Lynda Marie Jordan]], biochemist and associate professor of chemistry at [[North Carolina A&T State University]]
* [[Angie Turner King]], professor of chemistry and mathematics at [[West Virginia State University|West Virginia State College]]
* [[Evelyn Nicol]], [[Immunology|immunologist]], [[microbiologist]], and the first to isolate the [[Varicella zoster virus|herpes zoster virus]]
* [[E. E. O'Banion]], chairman of the chemistry department and director of the natural sciences department at [[Prairie View A&M University]] from the 1940s to the 1970s<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 10, 2003 |title=Scholarship at PVAMU in memory of O'Banion |url=https://www.chron.com/neighborhood/article/Scholarship-at-PVAMU-in-memory-of-O-Banion-9792261.php |access-date=September 8, 2024 |website=Chron}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Beta Kappa Chi Scientific Society, 1943–1953 (letter) |url=https://credo.library.umass.edu/view/pageturn/mums411-b008-f105/#page/11/mode/1up |access-date=September 8, 2024 |website=University of Massachusetts Amherst Library}}</ref><ref name=":10" />
* [[Joseph Alphonso Pierce]], mathematician and statistician
* [[Hildrus Poindexter]] (''Alpha''), [[bacteriologist]], pioneer in tropical medicine, and head of the department of preventative medicine, bacteriology, and public health at the [[Howard University College of Medicine]]<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":5"/><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":9" />
* [[Johnnie Hines Watts Prothro]], professor at the [[Tuskegee Institute]], [[University of Connecticut at Storrs]], and [[Georgia State University]]
* [[Carl Glennis Roberts]] (''Alpha''), one of the first African Americans to be elected to the [[American College of Surgeons]] and a president of the [[National Medical Association]]<ref name=":2" />
* [[Gladys W. Royal]], early African-American [[biochemist]]
* [[Alberta Jones Seaton]], professor of biology at [[Texas Southern University]] and the first African-American women awarded a [[doctorate]] in [[zoology]]
* [[Jerome Singleton]], [[Paralympic]] [[Track and field|athlete]]
* [[Frederick D. Stubbs]] (''Alpha''), [[thoracic surgeon]] in [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]]<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Topic {{!}} Dr. Frederick Douglas Stubbs, M.D., F.A.C.S. {{!}} The History of African Americans in the Medical Professions |url=https://chaamp.virginia.edu/node/4158 |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=CHAAMP (Consortium on the History of African Americans in the Medical Professions) |publisher=University of Virginia}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mahoney |first=Eleanor |date=2018-01-14 |title=Frederick D. Stubbs (1906–1947) |url=https://www.blackpast.org/african-american-history/stubbs-frederick-d-1906-1947/ |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=Black Past |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Frederick Douglass Stubbs |url=https://badahistory.net/view.php?ID=83 |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=Blacks@Dartmouth 1775 to 1960 |publisher=Black Alumni of Dartmouth Association}}</ref>
* [[Louise Nixon Sutton]], first chair of the Department of Physical Sciences and Mathematics at [[Elizabeth City State University]]
* [[Thyrsa Frazier Svager]], head of the Department of Mathematics at [[Central State University]]
* [[Thomas Wyatt Turner]] (''Alpha honorary''), botanist, head of the department of natural sciences at Howard University,  first Black American to receive a Ph.D. in [[botany]], and helped found the [[NAACP]] and the [[Federated Colored Catholics]]<ref name=":6" />
* [[Levi Watkins]], heart surgeon who was the first to successfully implant an automatic [[Defibrillation|defibrillator]] in a human patient
* [[I. J. K. Wells]] (''Alpha''), state supervisor of Negro schools for [[West Virginia]]<ref name=":5"/>
* [[Michael Duryea Williams]], professor at [[Clark Atlanta University]]
* [[James Edward Young]], professor physics at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]
